newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees rebuilding of east taking 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees rebuilding of east taking 15 years.

text.p: The German government expects the reconstruction of formerly communist east Germany to take at least 15 more years, economics state secretary Johannes Ludewig said on Thursday.
Setting up a functioning economic structure is taking longer than the six to seven years originally expected, and transfers will remain necessary, he told a news conference.
Bonn has spent over one trillion marks on transfers to the east since the two parts of Germany were unified in 1990.
The government must continue to pursue and active labour market policy in the east, and the west German business sector should become more involved, he said.
The main problem is that east German industrial parks are not up to standard, he said.

On Tuesday, the BvS, successor to Germany's Treuhand privatisation agency, said privatisation of former east German companies was proving more difficult than expected, but that it still hoped to complete its work by the end of 1998 as originally planned.
